- D39: prompt caching (explicit breakpoint on system + top-level automatic cache_control), and answered questions are trimmed to question + answer in the chat history (chat/agent.py).
- Data and docs/VALIDATION.md were regenerated; Daniel's ticks must be preserved.

Expected outcomes:
- Robinhood: 22 current, Campfire: 8 current.
- Robinhood VP count 15 (2 high, 13 medium, 0 low).
- John Glasgow has a "CEO & CFO" finance row backed by both the campfire.ai Doss blog post and the cfodive.com article.

Check whether D38 is applied correctly and no wider than intended. In particular:
- only real page dates, never retrieval dates, should drive promotions;
- sources.published_at stays NULL;
- no departed person became current.

Compare against `git show b215916:data/robinhood.com/leadership.json`.

**Part B (uncommitted, see `git status` / `git diff`).** Phase 6, the eval:
- eval/questions.yaml (22 cases)
- src/leadership/evaluate.py
- the `leadership eval` command in src/leadership/cli.py
- tests/test_eval.py
- the pyyaml dependency in pyproject.toml / uv.lock
- D40 in docs/DECISIONS.md
- eval/results.json and eval/RESULTS.md, from a real run: 22/22 passed

Spec: "8–10 Q&A per company with answers verified by hand; include the four example questions, at least two not-found, one follow-up, one conflict/low confidence; `leadership eval` runs them through the real agent and prints pass/fail; unit tests offline for title rules, evidence-snippet check, dedupe/resolve, repository queries."

Daniel also asked for these eval cases: no company given → asks which; an uncollected company → declines.

1. For every case in eval/results.json, check the agent's answer against the committed data and the case's `expected`. Flag any answer that passed but is factually wrong, or that a check would wrongly pass or fail.
2. Weak or over-fitted regexes.
3. Whether `expected` matches the data.
4. Rule compliance: no mocks in the runtime path, no secrets, parameterized SQL.

Run `.venv/Scripts/python.exe -I -m pytest -q` and `.venv/Scripts/ruff.exe check src tests`. Do NOT run the real eval or chat (costs money).

Report must-fix items versus nits, and end with PASS or FAIL.

tools.name: Read
tools.description:
Reads a file from the local filesystem.

- `file_path` must be an absolute path.
- Reads up to 2000 lines by default.
- When you already know which part of the file you need, only read that part. This can be important for larger files.
- Results are returned using cat -n format, with line numbers starting at 1
- Reads images (PNG, JPG, …) and presents them visually. Reads PDFs via the `pages` parameter (e.g. "1-5", max 20 pages/request; required for PDFs over 10 pages). Reads Jupyter notebooks (.ipynb) as cells with outputs.
- Reading a directory, a missing file, or an empty file returns an error or system reminder rather than content.
- Do NOT re-read a file you just edited to verify — Edit/Write would have errored if the change failed, and the harness tracks file state for you.

file_path.description: The absolute path to the file to read

offset.description: The line number to start reading from. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once

limit.description: The number of lines to read. Only provide if the file is too large to read at once.

pages.description: Page range for PDF files (e.g., "1-5", "3", "10-20"). Only applicable to PDF files. Maximum 20 pages per request.

allow_large.description: Set to true to read a text file, or a line range of one, that is over the usual size limits, up to what still fits in your context. Only use this when you genuinely need all of it or the user asked for the whole file; otherwise read it in parts with offset and limit, or search it.

tools.name: Grep
tools.description:
Content search built on ripgrep. Prefer this over `grep`/`rg` via Bash — results integrate with the permission UI and file links.

- Full regex syntax (e.g. "log.*Error", "function\s+\w+"). Ripgrep, not grep — escape literal braces (`interface\{\}`).
- Filter with `glob` (e.g. "**/*.tsx") or `type` (e.g. "js", "py", "rust").
- `output_mode`: "content" (matching lines), "files_with_matches" (paths only, default), or "count".
- `multiline: true` for patterns that span lines.

pattern.description: The regular expression pattern to search for in file contents

path.description: File or directory to search in (rg PATH). Defaults to current working directory.

glob.description: Glob pattern to filter files (e.g. "*.js", "*.{ts,tsx}") - maps to rg --glob

output_mode.description: Output mode: "content" shows matching lines (supports -A/-B/-C context, -n line numbers, head_limit), "files_with_matches" shows file paths (supports head_limit), "count" shows match counts (supports head_limit). Defaults to "files_with_matches".

-B.description: Number of lines to show before each match (rg -B). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-A.description: Number of lines to show after each match (rg -A). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

context.description: Number of lines to show before and after each match (rg -C). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise.

-n.description: Show line numbers in output (rg -n). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to true.

-o.description: Print only the matched (non-empty) parts of each matching line, one match per output line (rg -o / --only-matching). Requires output_mode: "content", ignored otherwise. Defaults to false.

type.description: File type to search (rg --type). Common types: js, py, rust, go, java, etc. More efficient than include for standard file types.

head_limit.description: Limit output to first N lines/entries, equivalent to "| head -N". Works across all output modes: content (limits output lines), files_with_matches (limits file paths), count (limits count entries). Defaults to 250 when unspecified. Pass 0 for unlimited (use sparingly — large result sets waste context).

offset.description: Skip first N lines/entries before applying head_limit, equivalent to "| tail -n +N | head -N". Works across all output modes. Defaults to 0.

multiline.description: Enable multiline mode where . matches newlines and patterns can span lines (rg -U --multiline-dotall). Default: false.

tools.name: Glob
tools.description: Fast file pattern matching. Supports glob patterns like "**/*.js" or "src/**/*.ts". Returns matching file paths sorted by modification time.

pattern.description: The glob pattern to match files against

path.description: The directory to search in. If not specified, the current working directory will be used. IMPORTANT: Omit this field to use the default directory. DO NOT enter "undefined" or "null" - simply omit it for the default behavior. Must be a valid directory path if provided.

tools.name: Bash

Executes a bash command and returns its output.

- `timeout` is in milliseconds: default 120000, max 600000 for a foreground command.

- Interactive flags (`-i`, e.g. `git rebase -i`, `git add -i`) are not supported in this environment.
- Use the `gh` CLI for GitHub operations (PRs, issues, API).

Author: Danilo Pangilinan <dpg2003@gmail.com>
Date:   Tue Nov 24 18:21:15 2026 -0800

    feat: seat split, roster dating, chat prompt caching (D37-D39)
    
    - D37: a C-level title naming several seats ("CEO & CFO") is one role row
      per seat with its own sources; Glasgow gains a CFO row. Counts unchanged.
    - D38: a current roster listing is dated by its retrieval date; a search
      copy of the company's roster is medium confidence. Robinhood VPs: 15
      (2 high, 13 medium, 0 low).
    - D39: prompt caching for system + tools + conversation tail; answered
      questions are trimmed to question + answer. CFO follow-up: 51.8k -> 15.3k
      prompt tokens, $0.110 -> $0.025.
    - Data and VALIDATION.md regenerated (ticks kept).
    
    Co-Authored-By: Claude Opus 5.5 <noreply@anthropic.com>

diff --git a/docs/DECISIONS.md b/docs/DECISIONS.md
index a7d46bf..2bdd434 100644
--- a/docs/DECISIONS.md
+++ b/docs/DECISIONS.md
@@ -333,3 +333,54 @@ All deterministic, in `pipeline/resolve.py`. The LLM only reports what a page sa
   - **Former roles of current people:** in `not_current`, a person who left that role but holds another says "STILL CURRENT in another role" and lists `current_roles`.
   - **Cost:** each answer's tokens and cost (from `extract.PRICES`) are logged and shown in the CLI.
 
+
+## D37. One role row per C-suite seat in a combined title (Daniel, after Phase 5)
+
+- **Rule (`resolve._role_keys`):** a C-level title naming several seats becomes one role row per seat. For example, "CEO & CFO" and "CEO, CFO and founder" give a CEO row (function `other`) and a CFO row (`finance`). Each row is resolved from the claims whose wording names that seat (`titles.seat_functions`), so the CFO row has both CFO sources and its own dates and currency. A founder part still adds a founder role (D23).
+- **Not split:**
+  - VP-level titles that name a C-suite title, e.g. "Vice President and Chief Information Security Officer". They stay one VP row (D30).
+  - General Counsel / Chief Legal titles, which D4 decides.
+- **Counts are people, not roles,** so they don't change: Campfire stays at 8 current and Robinhood at 22.
+- **Effect:**
+  - John Glasgow (Campfire) now has "CEO & CFO" (c_level/finance, current, last dated 2026-02-24), backed by the Campfire Doss blog post and the CFO Dive article, as well as "CEO & Founder".
+  - No Robinhood rows change.
+- The chat's `also_titled` (D36) is kept for VP-level wordings such as McHenry's and Koller's. Glasgow no longer appears there because his CFO row is resolved.
+- **Supersedes** D36's "Rejected for now: splitting combined titles".
+
+## D38. A current roster listing is dated by its retrieval date (Daniel, after Phase 5)
+
+- **Rule:**
+  - A current listing on the company's own leadership or team roster page has no page date. It is dated by its retrieval date (`Claim.effective_date`), not treated as undated, because a roster page shows current staff when it is fetched.
+  - A roster page is a listing whose last path segment is a people word (`validate.ROSTER_PATH`), on the company's own host: fetched directly, or a search copy of it.
+  - `/management/<name>` profile pages are not rosters.
+- **Confidence:** a search copy of the company's roster (investors.robinhood.com/governance/leadership is bot-blocked, D13) is `medium` on its own, not `low`. Corroboration raises it under the usual rules (an SEC filing, or 2+ sources including the company site, give `high`).
+- **Where the date is used:**
+  - the role's `as_of`, and the current-vs-former comparison;
+  - the 18-month rule (D32), so a roster listing is never stale;
+  - the proxy rule (D16): a C-level title on the current roster but not in the proxy stays current and stays listed for review, with the note "listed on the company's current roster (retrieved <date>)".
+  - Promotions (a newer title supersedes an older one) still use real page dates only. A retrieval date says when the page was read, not when a title started.
+- **Source records are unchanged:** sources.published_at stays NULL, because the page itself has no date. The chat marks such a source `dated_by: retrieval date (current roster page)`.
+- **Effect:**
+  - Robinhood: 13 people sourced only from the roster copy move from low to medium confidence, and roster roles are now dated 2026-11-24 (when the roster was retrieved). Current counts are unchanged at 22 and 8.
+  - The VP count is still 15: 2 high, 13 medium, 0 low (it was 2, 3 and 10).
+  - Campfire has no roster page in the data, so nothing changes there.
+
+## D39. Chat token use: prompt caching and trimmed history (Daniel, after Phase 5)
+
+- **Caching:**
+  - One explicit `cache_control` breakpoint on the system block caches the tool definitions with it, because tools render first.
+  - A top-level automatic `cache_control` caches the growing conversation within a question's tool loop.
+  - TTL is 5 minutes. Cost uses 1.25x for cache writes and 0.05x for cache reads on Sonnet 5.5 / Opus 5.5 (0.1x on other models).
+- **Trimming:** once a question is answered, its tool calls, tool results and thinking are replaced in `history` by one assistant message: the tools called, then the answer text. The answer already holds the facts and URLs a follow-up needs, and rule 1 makes the agent call tools again for anything new. `trim_history=False` and `prompt_cache=False` restore the old behaviour; the measurements use them.
+- **Measured on the real agent**, same 5 Robinhood questions (CTO, VPs, marketing, CEO location, "and the CFO?"):
+
+  | Question | Before: prompt tokens | Before: cost | After: prompt tokens (cached read) | After: cost |
+  |---|---:|---:|---:|---:|
+  | Who's their CTO? | 11,194 | $0.0315 | 11,173 (6,551) | $0.0220 |
+  | How many VPs? | 19,754 | $0.0482 | 15,362 (5,373) | $0.0350 |
+  | Who heads marketing? | 31,926 | $0.0696 | 10,335 (7,046) | $0.0160 |
+  | Where is their CEO based? | 62,356 | $0.1292 | 51,478 (30,384) | $0.0601 |
+  | **and the CFO?** | **51,813** | **$0.1104** | **15,345 (9,311)** | **$0.0250** |
+  | Total | 177,043 | $0.389 | 103,693 | $0.158 |
+
+- The CEO-location turn is still large because `get_person` for Vlad Tenev returns many facts. That is a possible later trim; it is not done here.

+## D37. One role row per C-suite seat in a combined title (Daniel, after Phase 5)
+
+- **Rule (`resolve._role_keys`):** a C-level title naming several seats becomes one role row per seat. For example, "CEO & CFO" and "CEO, CFO and founder" give a CEO row (function `other`) and a CFO row (`finance`). +  - VP-level titles that name a C-suite title, e.g. "Vice President and Chief Information Security Officer". They stay one VP row (D30).

+- **Effect:**
+  - John Glasgow (Campfire) now has "CEO & CFO" (c_level/finance, current, last dated 2026-02-24), backed by the Campfire Doss blog post and the CFO Dive article, as well as "CEO & Founder".
+  - No Robinhood rows change.
+- The chat's `also_titled` (D36) is kept for VP-level wordings such as McHenry's and Koller's. Glasgow no longer appears there because his CFO row is resolved.
+- **Supersedes** D36's "Rejected for now: splitting combined titles".
+
+## D38. A current roster listing is dated by its retrieval date (Daniel, after Phase 5)
+
+- **Rule:**
+  - A current listing on the company's own leadership or team roster page has no page date. It is dated by its retrieval date (`Claim.effective_date`), not treated as undated, because a roster page shows current staff when it is fetched.
+  - A roster page is a listing whose last path segment is a people word (`validate.ROSTER_PATH`), on the company's own host: fetched directly, or a search copy of it.
+  - `/management/<name>` profile pages are not rosters.
+- **Confidence:** a search copy of the company's roster (investors.robinhood.com/governance/leadership is bot-blocked, D13) is `medium` on its own, not `low`. Corroboration raises it under the usual rules (an SEC filing, or 2+ sources including the company site, give `high`).
+- **Where the date is used:**
+  - the role's `as_of`, and the current-vs-former comparison;
+  - the 18-month rule (D32), so a roster listing is never stale;
+  - the proxy rule (D16): a C-level title on the current roster but not in the proxy stays current and stays listed for review, with the note "listed on the company's current roster (retrieved <date>)".

if "company_site" in types or len(urls) >= 2 or any(c.roster for c in claims):
        return "medium"
    return "low"


def _resolve_role(
    key: tuple[str, str],
    claims: list[Claim],
    proxy_date: str | None,
    proxy_keys: set[tuple[str, str]],
    today: date,
) -> ResolvedRole:
    seniority, function = key
    claims = sorted(claims, key=_claim_sort_key)
    current = [c for c in claims if c.status != "former"]
    former = [c for c in claims if c.status == "former"]
    # D38: a roster listing counts as dated by its retrieval date (effective_date).
    newest_current = max((_ordinal(c.effective_date) for c in current), default=-1)
    newest_former = max((_ordinal(c.effective_date) for c in former), default=-1)
    newest_dated_current = max((_ordinal(c.published_at) for c in current), default=-1)
    note = ""
    retired_by_proxy = False
    # A 'former' statement wins unless a current claim is strictly newer (undated = oldest).
    is_current = bool(current) and (not former or newest_current > newest_former)
    if former and current:
        note = (
            f"sources disagree on whether this role is current: former per "
            f"{_cite(_newest(former))}; current per {_cite(_newest(current))}"
        )
    elif former:
        note = f"stated as former in {_cite(_newest(former))}"

    # D16 proxy rule: a dated C-level newsroom/search claim older than the latest proxy, for a
    # role the proxy doesn't list for this person, is not current. SEC claims are exempt.
    # Undated claims can't be shown to be older: they stay current and are listed for review
    # (the proxy lists only Section 16 officers, so e.g. a Chief People Officer may be absent).
    if (
        is_current
        and seniority == "c_level"
        and proxy_date is not None
        and key not in proxy_keys
        and not any(c.doc.source_type == "sec_filing" for c in current)
    ):
        roster = [c for c in current if c.roster]
        if roster:
            note = (
                f"C-level title not in the {proxy_date} proxy; listed on the company's current "
                f"roster: {_cite(roster[0])}"
            )
        elif newest_dated_current <= 0:
            note = (
                f"C-level title not in the {proxy_date} proxy; source is undated: "
                f"{_cite(current[0])}"
            )
        elif newest_dated_current < _ordinal(proxy_date):
            is_current = False
            retired_by_proxy = True
            note = (
                f"not listed in the {proxy_date} proxy, which is newer than this claim; "
                f"last confirmed in {_cite(_newest(current))}"
            )

    supporting = current if is_current or retired_by_proxy else (former or claims)
    dated = [c.effective_date for c in supporting if c.effective_date]
    as_of = max(dated) if dated else None
    confidence = role_confidence(supporting)
    single = len({c.doc.url for c in supporting}) == 1
    # The 18-month single-source rule (D32) is applied once, in retire_stale(), after rows
    # are deduped and merged, so pooled sources count as confirmation.
    # D22: evidence re-anchored from the source (not the model's own quote) is low unless
    # another source corroborates the role. (Listed in review.reanchored either way.)
    if single and all(c.affiliation == "byline" for c in supporting):
        confidence = "low"
        note = note or (
            f"affiliation rests on a single author byline on the company's site: "
            f"{_cite(supporting[0])}"
        )
    if single and all(c.reanchored for c in supporting):
        confidence = "low"
        note = note or (
            f"evidence re-anchored by name and title in one block; single source: "
            f"{_cite(supporting[0])}"
        )
    title = _title_claim(supporting).title
    return ResolvedRole(title, function, seniority, is_current, as_of, confidence, claims, note)


def _title_key(title: str) -> str:
    """'CEO & Founder' and 'ceo and founder' are the same title."""
    return " ".join(re.sub(r"[^a-z0-9 ]", " ", title.lower().replace("&", " and ")).split())


def dedupe_roles(roles: list[ResolvedRole]) -> list[ResolvedRole]:
    """D29: one row per (normalized title, function) per person; sources are merged.

    "CEO & Founder" resolves to a C-level role and a founder role (D4/D23); shown as two
    identical rows. The merged row keeps the most senior seniority, is current if either
    was, and keeps every claim, the newest as_of, the best confidence, and both notes."""
    groups: dict[tuple[str, str], list[ResolvedRole]] = {}
    for r in roles:
        groups.setdefault((_title_key(r.title), r.function), []).append(r)
    out = []
    for group in groups.values():
        if len(group) == 1:
            out.append(group[0])
            continue
        lead = min(group, key=lambda r: (not r.is_current, _SENIORITY_RANK[r.seniority]))
        claims = list({id(c): c for r in group for c in r.claims}.values())
        notes = [r.note for r in group if r.note]
        seniorities = sorted({r.seniority for r in group}, key=_SENIORITY_RANK.__getitem__)
        if len(seniorities) > 1:
            notes.append(f"one row for: {', '.join(seniorities)}")
        out.append(
            ResolvedRole(
                lead.title,
                lead.function,
                lead.seniority,
                any(r.is_current for r in group),
                max((r.as_of for r in group if r.as_of), default=None),
                max((r.confidence for r in group), key=_CONFIDENCE_RANK.__getitem__),
                claims,
                "; ".join(dict.fromkeys(notes)),
            )
        )
    return out


_TITLE_STOP = frozenset({"and", "of", "the", "llc", "inc", "for", "at", "to", "a"})
OVERLAP_MIN = 0.6  # Jaccard similarity of title words for "the wording mostly overlaps"


# Seniority words don't count toward overlap: "VP of Product" and "VP of Product Marketing"
# share only "product", so they stay two roles.
_SENIORITY_WORDS = frozenset(
    {"vp", "svp", "evp", "avp", "senior", "executive", "chief", "officer", "head"}
)


def _title_words(title: str) -> frozenset[str]:
    t = _title_key(title)
    t = re.sub(r"\bvice president\b", "vp", t)
    return frozenset(w for w in t.split() if w not in _TITLE_STOP | _SENIORITY_WORDS)


def title_overlap(a: str, b: str) -> float:
    wa, wb = _title_words(a), _title_words(b)
    if len(wa) < 2 or len(wb) < 2:
        return 0.0
    return len(wa & wb) / len(wa | wb)


def merge_overlapping_roles(
    roles: list[ResolvedRole],
) -> tuple[list[ResolvedRole], list[dict[str, Any]]]:
    """D30: rows of one person with the same seniority whose wording mostly overlaps are one
    role (Matt Billings: "VP and President of Robinhood Financial LLC and Robinhood
    Securities, LLC" and "Vice President, Brokerage and President, Robinhood Financial and
    Robinhood Securities"). The newest wording is kept (with its function); sources merged.
    Returns the rows and one record per merge, for VALIDATION.md."""
    rows = list(roles)
    merges: list[dict[str, Any]] = []
    changed = True
    while changed:
        changed = False
        for i, a in enumerate(rows):
            for b in rows[i + 1 :]:
                # Same seniority and the same currency: a former role is history, not a
                # duplicate of the current one.
                if (
                    a.seniority != b.seniority
                    or a.seniority == "founder"
                    or a.is_current != b.is_current
                ):
                    continue
                score = title_overlap(a.title, b.title)
                if score < OVERLAP_MIN:
                    continue
                claims = list({id(c): c for c in a.claims + b.claims}.values())
                newest = _title_claim(claims)
                keep = a if any(c is newest for c in a.claims) else b
                # The merged row has the sources of both: a "single source" note (18-month or
                # re-anchored) no longer applies, and confidence is recomputed from them.
                supporting = [c for c in claims if c.status != "former"] or claims
                multi = len({c.doc.url for c in supporting}) > 1
                notes = [
                    n for n in (a.note, b.note)
                    if n and not (multi and "single source" in n)
                ]  # fmt: skip
                notes.append(
                    f"merged from 2 rows with overlapping wording (D30): {a.title} / {b.title}"
                )
                confidence = max(
                    (a.confidence, b.confidence, role_confidence(supporting)),
                    key=_CONFIDENCE_RANK.__getitem__,
                )
                merged = ResolvedRole(
                    newest.title,
                    keep.function,
                    keep.seniority,
                    a.is_current,
                    max((r.as_of for r in (a, b) if r.as_of), default=None),
                    confidence,
                    claims,
                    "; ".join(dict.fromkeys(notes)),
                )
                merges.append(
                    {"kept": newest.title, "merged": sorted({a.title, b.title} - {newest.title}),
                     "overlap": round(score, 2), "seniority": keep.seniority}
                )  # fmt: skip
                rows = [r for r in rows if r is not a and r is not b] + [merged]
                changed = True
                break
            if changed:
                break
    return rows, merges


def retire_stale(roles: list[ResolvedRole], today: date) -> None:
    """D32, from Daniel's hand-check (all 8 such Robinhood records had departed): a current
    role whose only source is older than 18 months is NOT current unless a newer source
    confirms it. Runs after rows are merged, so a merged row's pooled sources count as
    confirmation. Founder roles are exempt (D23 decides their currency); undated sources
    can't be shown to be old and are left alone."""
    for r in roles:
        if not r.is_current or r.seniority == "founder" or not r.as_of:
            continue
        supporting = [c for c in r.claims if c.status != "former"] or r.claims
        if len({c.doc.url for c in supporting}) != 1:
            continue
        if (today - date.fromisoformat(r.as_of)).days <= STALE_AFTER_DAYS:
            continue
        r.is_current = False
        r.confidence = "low"
        stale = (
            f"single source, last confirmed {r.as_of} in {_cite(supporting[0])}; no newer "
            f"confirmation (older than 18 months)"
        )
        r.note = f"{stale}; {r.note}" if r.note else stale

    def __init__(self, fetcher: Fetcher, max_results: int = MAX_RESULTS) -> None:
        self.fetcher = fetcher
        self.max_results = max_results
        self.api_calls = 0

    def _search(self, query: str) -> dict:
        key = hashlib.sha256(query.encode("utf-8")).hexdigest()[:20]
        path = self.fetcher.cache_dir / NAMESPACE / "_queries" / f"{key}.json"
        if path.exists() and not self.fetcher.refresh:
            data = json.loads(path.read_text(encoding="utf-8"))
            if _drop_excluded(data):
                _write_json(path, data)  # purge text from newly excluded domains
            return data
        payload = {
            "query": query,
            "search_depth": "basic",
            "max_results": self.max_results,
            "include_raw_content": "text",
            "exclude_domains": list(EXCLUDED_DOMAINS),
        }
        headers = {"Authorization": f"Bearer {require_setting('TAVILY_API_KEY')}"}
        self.api_calls += 1
        resp = httpx.post(TAVILY_URL, json=payload, headers=headers, timeout=60)
        if resp.status_code != 200:
            # Don't cache failures; the error body never contains the key.
            raise RuntimeError(f"Tavily search failed (HTTP {resp.status_code}): {resp.text[:200]}")
        data = {"query": query, "fetched_at": utc_now_iso(), "response": resp.json()}
        _drop_excluded(data)
        _write_json(path, data)
        return data

    def discover(self, company: Company) -> AdapterReport:
        report = AdapterReport(SOURCE_TYPE)
        seen: set[str] = set()
        for query in build_queries(company):
            data = self._search(query)
            results = data["response"].get("results", [])
            for url in data.get("excluded_urls", []):
                if url not in seen:
                    seen.add(url)
                    report.skip(url, "excluded domain (ToS)")
                    self.fetcher.text_path(NAMESPACE, url).unlink(missing_ok=True)
            if not results:
                report.notes.append(f"no results for {query!r}")
            for r in results:
                url = r.get("url", "")
                if not url or url in seen:
                    continue
                seen.add(url)
                if is_excluded(url):
                    report.skip(url, "excluded domain (ToS)")
                    # Don't keep (or commit) text from a domain excluded after it was cached.
                    self.fetcher.text_path(NAMESPACE, url).unlink(missing_ok=True)
                    continue
                direct_fetch = ""
                if is_company_host(url, company):
                    direct_fetch = self._direct_fetch_status(url)
                    if direct_fetch.startswith("disallowed"):
                        report.skip(url, f"company robots.txt {direct_fetch} (D13)")
                        self.fetcher.text_path(NAMESPACE, url).unlink(missing_ok=True)
                        continue
                text = (r.get("raw_content") or r.get("content") or "").strip()
                if len(text) < 100:
                    report.skip(url, "search result has no usable text")
                    continue
                lines = (" ".join(line.split()) for line in text.splitlines())
                text = "\n".join(line for line in lines if line)
                raw_path = self.fetcher.write_text(NAMESPACE, url, text)
                report.documents.append(
                    RawDocument(
                        url=url,
                        source_type=SOURCE_TYPE,
                        title=r.get("title", ""),
                        text=text,
                        fetched_at=data["fetched_at"],
                        raw_path=raw_path,

                            "query": query,
                            "score": r.get("score"),
                            "published_date": r.get("published_date"),
                            "raw_content": bool(r.get("raw_content")),
                        }
                        | ({"direct_fetch": direct_fetch} if direct_fetch else {}),

+## D40. Phase 6: the eval
+
+- **`eval/questions.yaml`:** 10 cases per company, plus 2 run with no company selected. They cover:
+  - the four example questions;
+  - two or more not-found questions per company (salary, email, revenue, age);
+  - a follow-up per company;
+  - a source conflict (Warnick);
+  - low confidence (Campfire's VPs, Nick Jezienicki);
+  - a review flag (Koegel);
+  - the company-handling cases: no company selected (asks which), an uncollected company (Stripe, declined), and an uncollected company asked about inside a Robinhood chat.
+- **Expected answers:**
+  - `expected` is written from the committed data.
+  - `verified_by` is null until Daniel hand-checks a case. `leadership eval` prints how many are unverified.
+- **Grading is deterministic:** regex include and exclude checks on the last answer, required tool calls with arguments, `no_tools`, and "cites a tool-result URL". The same answer always gets the same verdict, and every failure names the check that failed.
+  - **Rejected: an LLM judge.** It is non-deterministic, adds cost, and a second model would grade the first.
+  - **Weakness:** regexes can reject a correct paraphrase. In the first run, "Stripe isn't one of the companies in the collected data" failed the decline pattern, so the pattern was widened. Exclude patterns target the specific wrong claim (for example "Pinner is the current CTO") rather than a name, because a correct answer mentions the former holder.
+- **Running it:** `leadership eval [domain]` runs that company's cases plus the no-company cases, 4 cases in parallel, through the real agent. It writes `eval/results.json` and `eval/RESULTS.md` (the answers, the tools called, and the cost), and exits with status 1 if any case fails.
+- **Result:** 22/22 passed with claude-sonnet-5-5, costing $0.21.
+- **Dependency:** PyYAML, for the spec's `questions.yaml`.

def _reply(text, steps=(), sources=()):
    return SimpleNamespace(text=text, steps=list(steps), sources=list(sources))


def _step(tool, **args):
    return SimpleNamespace(tool=tool, input=args)


def test_grader_include_exclude_tools_and_citations():
    case = {"checks": {"include": ["Paul Nichols"], "exclude": ["San Martin is the CTO"],

9:You are a senior engineer helping me build a take-home for an AI engineering role. Reviewers will clone the repo and run it. They are evaluating:
21:1. **Collection pipeline**: find the company's leadership (C-level, VPs, Heads of departments) from public sources, collect public profile data, and store it with provenance.
22:2. **Chat interface**: an LLM-powered chat over the stored data that answers questions like "Who's their CTO?", "How many VPs do they have?", "Who heads marketing?", "Where is their CEO based?"
30:- Ship an `.env.example`, never real keys.
35:- **Never invent data.** If there's no evidence, the field stays NULL. The chat agent says "not found in the collected data" and, where useful, says what sources were checked. It never guesses.
44:3. **One web search API** (Tavily, Brave, or Serper; pick one and justify it). Use targeted queries (`"{company}" VP`, `"{company}" "head of"`, `"{company}" CTO`) to find press releases, news, and conference bios, which is where most VPs and department heads appear.
50:Rationale (put this in `docs/DECISIONS.md`): the target questions are structured (filter by role, count VPs, look up a location), so a relational model answers them exactly. A vector store would make counts and filters less reliable. SQLite keeps it clone-and-go, and a plain `schema.sql` stays Postgres-compatible.
56:                -- function: engineering|product|finance|marketing|sales|operations|legal|people|security|design|data|other
86:  - Say "not found" when the data isn't there.
88:- Keep conversation history so follow-ups work ("where is *she* based?").
93:- **Sidebar:** company selector, plus last-run stats (date, sources used, people found, LLM cost).
101:**CLI** (Typer + Rich): `leadership collect <url>`, `leadership chat <domain>`, `leadership eval <domain>`, `leadership ui`. Collection runs from the CLI, not from the UI.
111:- **Fresh-clone test:** clone → `uv sync` → copy `.env.example` → F5 **Launch UI** must work against the committed data with only `ANTHROPIC_API_KEY` set.
113:Dependencies: Python 3.12, `httpx`, `trafilatura` (or `selectolax`), `pydantic`, `anthropic`, `streamlit`, `typer`, `rich`, `python-dotenv`. Justify anything else.
124:eval/questions.yaml
130:README.md  .env.example  .gitattributes  pyproject.toml  .vscode/  .streamlit/
135:- **`docs/VALIDATION.md`**: after collection, generate a checklist for each company: every person, title, location, and source URL, with a blank "Verified by Daniel: ✅ / ❌ / note" column. I'll hand-check each row against its source. Then record the errors I found, what caused each one, and what we changed to fix it. Also record **known misses**: leaders I found manually that the pipeline didn't.
136:- **`eval/questions.yaml`**: 8–10 Q&A per company, with answers I've verified by hand. Include:
137:  - the four example questions,
138:  - at least two questions the data **can't** answer, where the correct answer is "not found",
139:  - one follow-up question,
141:- `leadership eval` runs them through the real agent and prints pass/fail.
142:- **Unit tests** (offline, no keys): title rules, the evidence-snippet check, dedupe/resolve, and repository queries.
152:- How I validated the output, linking `VALIDATION.md` and eval results.
169:      - Generate `VALIDATION.md` with an "Agent verdict" column next to my blank "Verified by Daniel" column, and a "Known misses" section.
172:   6. Eval + tests.
190:| `fresh-clone-tester` | Before submission | Clones the committed repo into a temp folder, follows the README literally, and runs tests, eval, and a UI health check |

## Phase review: D37–D39 (89101bd) + Phase 6 eval (uncommitted)
**Verdict:** PASS WITH FIXES (no blockers, so PASS once the should-fix items below are done)
Tests: 208 passed / 0 failed · Ruff: `ruff check src tests` reports no issues, and `ruff format --check` reports "34 files already formatted"

### Blockers
None.
- No secrets. The only env file tracked is `.env.example`, and the grep for `sk-ant-` and `api_key=` found nothing.
- There are no mocks in the runtime path. `evaluate.run_case` builds a real `ChatAgent`, and the fakes in `tests/test_eval.py` are `SimpleNamespace` objects.
- The eval adds no SQL.
- The only broad `except` is `evaluate.py:111`. It records the error as a failed case and keeps `repr(exc)`, so nothing is hidden.

### Part A: what I confirmed (D37/D38)
- **Expected outcomes all hold.**
  - Robinhood has 22 current, Campfire 8.
  - Robinhood has 15 current VPs: 2 high (Moskowitz, Billings), 13 medium, 0 low.
  - Glasgow has `("CEO & CFO", c_level, finance, current, 2026-02-24)` alongside "CEO & Founder". Its sources are the campfire.ai Doss post and the cfodive.com article.
- **No change of currency.** I diffed `b215916:data/*/leadership.json` against HEAD.
  - Robinhood: 44 people before and after, and no `is_current` flips.
  - The only changes are 13 low→medium confidence moves and `as_of` moving to 2026-11-24 on rows backed by the roster. That includes Shiv Verma (2026-07-29 → 2026-11-24), Gallagher, Quirk, Tenev, Moskowitz and Billings.
  - Campfire: the only change is Glasgow's new CFO row. Nobody who left became current.
- **Promotions use page dates only.** `resolve.py:536` and `:544` use `c.published_at`, and `_title_claim` (`:196`) also orders by `published_at`. A row backed only by the roster can neither supersede a role nor be superseded.
- **`sources.published_at` stays NULL.** In the read-only DB, `investors.robinhood.com/governance/leadership` shows `published_at=None`. It is the only roster source in either DB.
- **Daniel's ticks are preserved.** In the VALIDATION.md diff, only the confidence, title and note columns changed. Every ✅ cell is identical.

### Should fix
1. **[validate.py:67, DECISIONS.md:353-354] D38 dates a search copy by the time of the Tavily query, not by when the page showed those people.** `search.py:119` sets `"fetched_at": utc_now_iso()` when the query is made, but the text is Tavily's indexed `raw_content`, whose crawl date is unknown. So "current roster, retrieved 2026-11-24" claims more than we know.
   - It also reaches `resolve.py:307-313`: a roster claim now beats any dated "former" claim, and D32 can never retire it.
   - No data changed because of this, and Daniel live-checked the page on Nov 23, which limits the risk.
   - Fix: say in D38 that, for a search copy, the date is when the search was made and the date of the content is unknown. Label it "search copy, retrieved …" in `_cite` and `dated_by`.
2. **[tests/test_extract_resolve.py] Nothing tests the two D38 boundaries you asked about.** No test shows that an undated roster VP row does not supersede a dated title (and is not superseded). No test covers a roster claim against a dated `former` claim. Fix: add one small test for each, so the "page dates only" rule is pinned.
3. **[eval/questions.yaml:43, 162, 172, 222] The bare regex `"low"` matches "below" and "follow".** The rh-vps answer passes it through "All titles below come from…". Separately, `"confirmed"` is generic, so the rh-vps check would pass "15 VPs … 3 low confidence". Fix: use `"\\b0\\b low"` / `"0 low confidence"` for rh-vps, and `"\\blow confidence\\b"` elsewhere.
4. **[eval/questions.yaml:126] In rh-koegel-flag, `"still|current"` matches "no longer current".** A wrong "No, he has left" answer that mentions Klarna and Dec 31 would pass. Fix: `"\\b(yes|still (a )?current)\\b"`, plus exclude `"no longer|not current|has left"`.
5. **[eval/questions.yaml:81] rh-followup-cfo doesn't test the follow-up.** "and the CFO?" after a location question means "where is the CFO based?", and `expected` says the location isn't in the data. The only include is `"Shiv Verma"`, which an answer with no context also passes. Fix: add `"not found"` to the includes.
6. **[eval/questions.yaml, all 22 cases] `verified_by: null` everywhere.** The spec says "answers I've verified by hand". D40 discloses this and the CLI counts unverified cases, but Daniel has to fill these in before sign-off. That is a human step, not a code defect.

### Factual check of results.json
I checked all 22 answers against the committed data. Names, titles, dates, confidence and flags match, including Koegel's flag "decided_by Daniel, 2026-11-23". Every `expected` matches the data. One minor inaccuracy passed:
- **rh-marketing.** It says Deepak Rao's leadership page and his `/management/deepak-rao` bio page were "Both … last confirmed 2026-11-24, the retrieval date of the current roster page". The profile page is not a roster (`test_profile_page_is_not_a_roster`), and its `published_at` is None. No check covers this, and it is low impact.

### Nits
- `validate.py:101` `ROSTER_PATH` repeats `resolve.py:174` `_LISTING_PATH` character for character. Import one from the other.
- The `titles.py:167-168` `seat_functions` docstring still says "Resolution keeps one role row per title, filed under its first seat", which D37 now contradicts.
- `evaluate.py:114` is a runtime `assert reply is not None`. `load_cases` doesn't reject `turns: []`, so validate that instead.
- `evaluate.select` accepts an unknown domain without complaint. `leadership eval foo.com` silently runs only the 2 no-company cases.
- cf-founders: `list_leaders(seniority=founder)` misses Glasgow because D29 merges his founder row into the c_level row. The agent says so honestly and recovers with a second call, but the tool gap predates this phase and is worth noting.

### What's good
- Grading is deterministic, and every failure names the check that failed. The exclude patterns target the specific wrong claim (`Pinner is … cto`) rather than the name, so correct answers that mention former holders still pass.
- D40 openly records that the decline regex was widened after the first run, which is good provenance.
- The D38 change is narrow in the code. Promotions and `sources.published_at` are untouched, and the before/after data diff shows no currency flips.

**Final: PASS** (no blockers; fix items 1–5 and get Daniel's `verified_by` before human sign-off)

Files: `C:\Users\pangi\RAG Assignment\eval\questions.yaml`, `C:\Users\pangi\RAG Assignment\src\leadership\evaluate.py`, `C:\Users\pangi\RAG Assignment\src\leadership\pipeline\validate.py`, `C:\Users\pangi\RAG Assignment\src\leadership\pipeline\resolve.py`, `C:\Users\pangi\RAG Assignment\src\leadership\pipeline\titles.py`, `C:\Users\pangi\RAG Assignment\docs\DECISIONS.md`, `C:\Users\pangi\RAG Assignment\tests\test_extract_resolve.py`.

I wrote two temporary copies of the old JSON (`rh_old.json`, `cf_old.json`) to `C:\Users\pangi\AppData\Local\Temp\claude\3045e6618275fcfe\2b6f9504-dc65-4610-9e7a-ac2836aaf953\scratchpad\` for the diff. Nothing in the repo was touched.
